CFML Language Reference: Functions

ArrayLen

Returns the length of an array: the position of its last element. For a two- or three-dimensional array it returns the length of the first dimension.

Category

Array functions

Syntax

ArrayLen(array)

Parameters

array
The array to measure.

Returns

The number of elements as an integer.

Usage

ArrayLen is what you use as the TO value of an index CFLOOP over an array.

For a two-dimensional array, ArrayLen(Grid) is the number of rows and ArrayLen(Grid[2]) the number of columns in row 2. Rows may have different lengths.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- A small two-dimensional array: 2 rows, 3 columns --->
<CFSET Grid = ArrayNew(2)>
<CFSET Grid[1][1] = "A1"><CFSET Grid[1][2] = "B1"><CFSET Grid[1][3] = "C1">
<CFSET Grid[2][1] = "A2"><CFSET Grid[2][2] = "B2"><CFSET Grid[2][3] = "C2">

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>ArrayLen(Grid) = #ArrayLen(Grid)# rows,
ArrayLen(Grid[1]) = #ArrayLen(Grid[1])# columns.</P>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=4>
<CFLOOP INDEX="r" FROM="1" TO="#ArrayLen(Grid)#">
  <TR><CFLOOP INDEX="c" FROM="1" TO="#ArrayLen(Grid[r])#"><TD>#Grid[r][c]#</TD></CFLOOP></TR>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

ArrayNew, ArrayIsEmpty, ArrayResize, ListLen
